title: FT-Transformer: Resilient and Reliable Transformer with End-to-End Fault Tolerant Attention
problem: Transformer inference on large-scale HPC systems must handle soft errors (unavoidable at exascale). Existing operation-level fault tolerance introduces significant computational and memory overhead, reducing protection efficiency and limiting scalability.
motivation: Large-scale transformer inference requires fault tolerance, but existing frameworks protect individual operations, creating redundancy and overhead. Module-level protection could reduce overhead while maintaining coverage.
method: FT-Transformer implements module-level fault tolerance by treating attention module operations as single kernel with end-to-end protection. For linear modules, designs strided algorithm-based fault tolerance (ABFT) avoiding inter-thread communication.
key_novelty: Module-level (attention kernel) unified protection vs. operation-level; end-to-end fault tolerance across multi-step computations; strided ABFT for linear layers avoiding synchronization; 7.56x speedup over traditional methods.
contributions: Module-level fault tolerance architecture for transformer attention
End-to-end protection spanning multi-step attention computations
Strided ABFT algorithm for linear modules with minimal communication
7.56x speedup over operation-level fault tolerance with 13.9% average overhead
limitations: Abstract-only evaluation; specific transformer sizes/architectures not mentioned; scalability to largest models unclear; inference-only (no training)
primary_theme: Module-Level Fault Tolerance for Transformer Inference
